findings.content: STDOUT_JSON mode skips the VERDICT_OUTPUT_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES guard. `_read_output_file` (line 583) enforces the 1 MB cap for FILE_JSON mode, but the STDOUT_JSON branch uses `completed.stdout` directly from `_communicate`, which accumulates chunks without any size bound. A misbehaving adapter can produce arbitrarily large stdout and exhaust memory or inflate stored artifacts without triggering the limit.

`_read_cell_file_metadata` reads the file from the current working tree regardless of `review_commit`. The returned `line_count` is then used in `_validated_comments_for_cell` (line 635) to hard-fail any comment whose `end_line` exceeds it. When `review_commit` points to an older commit where the file was longer, valid line references are incorrectly rejected; when the file has since grown, out-of-range references incorrectly pass. The metadata should be derived from the commit being reviewed.

findings.content: subprocess.TimeoutExpired is not caught in _read_cell_file_metadata. When `timeout=10` is specified in subprocess.run, a TimeoutExpired exception can be raised if the git command takes too long. The except clause only catches CalledProcessError, so TimeoutExpired propagates uncaught as a raw exception instead of being wrapped in a ReviewAdapterError. This breaks the contract that callers can rely on ReviewAdapterError for all git-related failures.

The sentinel string used in _expand for brace escaping is constructed by concatenating a null-byte wrapper with 'OPEN'/'CLOSE'. If any variable value injected during substitution itself contains the sentinel prefix '\x00REVIEW_GAUNTLET_LITERAL_BRACE\x00', the final replace pass will incorrectly convert it to a literal brace character, corrupting the expanded output. There is no validation that expanded variable values are free of the sentinel before performing the suffix replacements.

Busy-wait loop after stdout thread finishes: the loop joins only `threads[0]`, so once stdout reading ends, every subsequent iteration returns immediately (0-second wait) and spins until stderr finishes. Under a high-volume review this causes 100% CPU usage on the polling thread until the stderr reader drains.

No file-size guard before reading the entire source file into memory. `file_path.read_bytes()` will load arbitrarily large files; the `VERDICT_OUTPUT_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` constant only protects verdict output. A multi-GB file passed as a review cell would exhaust process memory before any size check is possible.

`self._review_commit` is interpolated directly into the git-show argument without any format validation. A value such as `HEAD~1 -- /etc/passwd` or a ref containing shell-unsafe characters (even with `shell=False`, git itself interprets the ref) could produce unexpected git behavior or read files outside the intended commit. The field should be validated as a hex SHA or a safe ref name before use.

File content is read entirely into memory before the size check, creating an OOM risk. A buggy or malicious adapter could write an arbitrarily large verdict file that exhausts heap memory before the `VERDICT_OUTPUT_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` guard on line 614 can reject it. Check the file size via `output_path.stat().st_size` before reading.

`assert` is used to guard `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` being non-None. Python's `-O` / `-OO` flags strip all `assert` statements at compile time, so these checks silently disappear in optimised deployments. Replace with an explicit `if`/raise to keep the guard unconditional.

findings.content: `item.get("input", "")` uses a default of `""`, but `dict.get(key, default)` only returns the default when the key is absent — not when the key is present with value `None`. If Pydantic stores `input: None` in the error dict (which can happen for certain validation paths), this expression evaluates to `str(None)` = `"None"` (the 4-char string) and passes it to `_line_column_position` as the source text. The position computed from the tiny "None" string is almost always wrong or `None`, giving a misleading snippet window in the failure report.

findings.content: `_line_column_position` validates that `line <= len(lines)` but never checks that `column <= len(lines[line - 1])`. If the error message claims a column number beyond the actual line length, the returned byte offset falls into the following line's content. `_raw_snippet` then centres its window on the wrong location, producing a misleading error snippet.

TOCTOU race condition in size validation: `stat().st_size` is checked at line 606 before the file is read at line 625. A verdict file that is within the size limit at stat-time but grows between the two calls will bypass the `VERDICT_OUTPUT_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` guard. The validated size may not correspond to the content that is ultimately returned and written to `verdict.raw.json`. The fix is to read the raw bytes first, validate their length, then decode — eliminating the window between check and use.

STDOUT_JSON mode has no size limit on `completed.stdout`, while FILE_JSON mode enforces `VERDICT_OUTPUT_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` via `_read_output_file`. A misbehaving adapter can emit unbounded stdout, consuming unlimited memory without any guard.

`self._fixtures.get(cell.id) or self._fixtures.get(cell.file_path)` uses truthiness rather than an explicit `None` check. If a fixture intentionally maps `cell.id` to an empty list `[]` (meaning "no comments for this cell"), the falsy empty list causes the expression to fall through to the `cell.file_path` lookup, potentially applying the wrong fixture data.

findings.content: In `_communicate`, the poll loop only joins `threads[0]` (the stdout reader). When stdout closes before stderr, `threads[0].join(timeout=0.05)` returns immediately every iteration, causing a 100% CPU busy-wait until the stderr thread finishes. No test exercises the case where stderr outlives stdout (e.g. a command that writes nothing to stdout but emits large stderr), so this defect has no test evidence.

The `quiet_timeout_seconds` path (`_QuietTimeoutExpired`) has no test coverage through the public adapter API. `test_command_adapter_timeout_failure` covers absolute timeout (`timeout_seconds`) but there is no analogous test that runs a command that produces initial output and then goes silent, triggering the quiet-timeout branch and verifying partial stdout/stderr are saved to artifacts.

findings.content: Busy-wait when only stderr thread is still alive. The loop condition `any(t.is_alive() for t in threads)` stays True while stderr runs, but `threads[0].join(timeout=0.05)` returns immediately once the stdout thread is already dead. This causes a tight spin loop consuming 100% CPU until stderr finishes or a timeout fires.

STDOUT_JSON mode has no size limit on the verdict, while FILE_JSON mode enforces `VERDICT_OUTPUT_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES` (1 MB) via `_read_output_file`. A runaway or adversarial subprocess could produce unbounded stdout, causing OOM or excessive memory use before the parse step.

`init --worktree`、`init --git-worktree`、`finalize --merge` の各オプションがドキュメントに記載されていますが、このコミット時点の実際の CLI コードには存在しません。`src/review_gauntlet/cli.py` の `init` サブパーサーには `--from`、`--to`、`--commit`、`--all` しかなく、`finalize` サブパーサーにも `--merge` オプションはありません。ユーザーがこれらのコマンドを実行するとエラーになります。

`run` は通常の進行コマンドです。`review` の constitution に基づく動作は変わりません: `review` は 1 回の呼び出しで正確に 1 バッチだけ進め、`run` は外部エージェント経由で繰り返し ready タスクを実行します。`finalize` はクリーンアップコマンドではなくゲートです。必要なカバレッジが完了し、live findings が閉じられるまで失敗します。誤った `init` を破棄する場合だけ `cancel` を使ってください。`cancel` はセッションを `cancelled` として記録し、アクティブセッションのマーカーを削除しますが、チェックポイントは作成しません。","existing_code":"```bash

# ブランチまたは範囲をレビュー
review-gauntlet init --from main --to HEAD

# リポジトリ全体をレビュー
review-gauntlet init --all

# 推奨: アクティブセッションが finalize されるまで ready タスクを実行

# デバッグや監査結果の確認

review-gauntlet findings

# 誤った init を破棄する場合。チェックポイントは作成しない
review-gauntlet cancel

# オプション: Git ブランチとリンク worktree を作成してセッションを分離
review-gauntlet init --git-worktree
review-gauntlet run
review-gauntlet finalize --merge

`run` は通常の進行コマンドです。`review` の constitution に基づく動作は変わりません: `review` は 1 回の呼び出しで正確に 1 バッチだけ進め、`run` は外部エージェント経由で繰り返し ready タスクを実行します。`finalize` はクリーンアップコマンドではなくゲートです。必要なカバレッジが完了し、live findings が閉じられるまで失敗します。誤った `init` を破棄する場合だけ `cancel` を使ってください。`cancel` はセッションを `cancelled` として記録し、アクティブセッションのマーカーを削除しますが、チェックポイントは作成しません。

findings.content: TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) in `_read_output_file`: `stat().st_size` is checked before the file is read, leaving a window where the file could grow between the check and the read. This is inconsistent with the STDOUT_JSON path (lines 325-326) which checks `len(completed.stdout.encode("utf-8"))` *after* the data is already in memory. The stat-then-read pattern provides a false size guarantee and could allow a race-condition write to bypass the size limit.

Imprecise comments bypass all line-range validation, including the basic invariant check (`start_line < 1` or `end_line < start_line`). If an imprecise comment carries semantically invalid line numbers (e.g. `start_line=0`), they pass through unchecked and are inserted into the accepted tuple returned to callers. Downstream consumers that read those line numbers without their own guards will encounter out-of-range values.
